headline: Funding flows. Collaborations grow. Delays persist.
deck: This week, space funding continues to surge while strategic partnerships form amid ongoing delays.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid co-orbital concerns
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This round underscores the increasing urgency for co-orbital security solutions, as evidenced by the U.S. government's heightened focus on space domain awareness. With the Department of Defense's appetite for innovative defense tech, True Anomaly is well-positioned for growth.
stories.soWhat: In space, cash often trumps actual innovation, and True Anomaly is cashing in on a hot topic.

stories.head: UK and Florida pledge $400,000 for space projects
stories.body: The UK and Florida have committed $400,000 towards joint space projects, showcasing a rare instance of state-level collaboration in the space sector. This funding will likely focus on technology development that benefits both regions, but the small amount raises questions about the scale of ambition behind the partnership.
stories.soWhat: When collaboration comes with a price tag, it’s worth wondering if the return will justify the investment.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle test slips again
stories.body: For the third consecutive quarter, a hypersonic glide-vehicle test has been postponed, highlighting the persistent challenges in this high-stakes domain. The delays reflect not just technical hurdles but also a broader trend of overpromising and underdelivering in defense tech.
stories.soWhat: If hypersonic tech is the future of warfare, we might need to recalibrate our expectations—and timelines.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With $190 million in fresh capital, True Anomaly's next steps could reshape co-orbital security strategies.

watchlist.title: Watch for KBR's Golden Dome unit developments
watchlist.body: KBR's new defense tech unit may signal an aggressive push into military contracts, particularly in the Golden Dome project.

watchlist.title: Agile Space's new CTO could shift strategy
watchlist.body: The appointment of a new CTO at Agile Space Industries might indicate a strategic pivot or renewed focus on their tech offerings.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program suggests ongoing government reliance on data analytics for defense operations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
